summary: A page paints a picture on a canvas with Vello, on WebGPU or the CPU, and the painter's stage holds all picture motion in Rust, so the DOM motion modules go and the SVG stays as the semantic layer and the export.

value.name: Picture motion
value.responsibility: Turns one scene into the next as a pure function of a progress value: it pairs groups by subject id and mixes their typed geometry, opacity and transforms
value.description: The entrance, the departure, the far swap and the flight into a card follow the same rule. Nothing here draws, reads a clock or keeps state between frames, so the same inputs give the same items. The durations come from @archboard/timing through the page. flight.rs holds what moves a whole picture: a flight from the last picture, a part-by-part entrance, a leaving picture, the ghost of one that left, and the board inside a card that the camera flies into.

changes.value: One TanStack Router route at /, whose search parameters paneA, paneB and pane are the workspace, with repoA and repoB beside them naming each pane's repository by its identity or an untracked vault's registry name, never by a path. It is never legacy board authority. Canonical model, scope, and checkpoint parameters describe each open pane directly, including unavailable readings. Pane closure removes those parameters. Grammar changes retain the preceding architecture scope, focus, and filters. Unavailable flow identities remain explicit. History restores unavailable requested states without silently selecting Current. Explicit canonical addresses remain visible when the server remembers a legacy board. issues.mine: It writes the picture into the surface once per picture: the SVG that stays in the page under the canvas as the hidden semantic layer (picture-transition.ts). It tells the stage how the picture arrives, cut to, carried on from the last or brought in part by part, and how far the cards the two pictures share have moved; the painter does the motion. Flights read the time and their frames from the frame clock. The picture of a board that a flight into a card arrived at is put up as it is, with no entrance.
issues.theirs: It writes the picture into the surface itself, once per picture, and runs the traffic of each picture, ghost and borrowed group as it puts them up. Flights read the time and their frames from the frame clock, and the picture clock its traffic runs on is read and set through it, so a replay seeks every one of them to the frame's time. The picture of a model that a flight into a card arrived at is put up as it is, with no entrance. Continuing cards carry their one shared chip and moving words; content comparison ignores the per-picture placement properties, so a moved card keeps its shared content (picture-pairing.ts).

issues.mine:
It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, no painter is still starting, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

A canonical talk draws its captured model and narrative through the shared walkthrough presentation. It reads no mutable vault and needs no source repository for replay.
